By: Hein Kaiser | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we investigate how a luxury car scam fleeced almost R 200 million from victim's pockets.

Unique Selling Point:
Its a multi layered ponzi and fraud scheme, it's sexy and driven by status, ego and cash... a festival of robbing Peter to pay Paul and then robbing Paul to pay another.

Summary:
It’s fraud, on a grand scale. Two schemes so elaborate and hundreds of millions of Rand that have magically disappeared.

Imagine driving a luxury car, like an Aston Martin, and you do not have to pay the massive instalments that goes with it. Now imagine, that you get to drive an Aston Martin this month, a Ferrari the next, and a Porche the month after that. For 900 investors, this was their dream come true. All they had to do was ‘buy’ a middleweight car, which was ‘rented out’ to someone else, that covered off the instalments, and the luxury car experience was theirs….. It sounds bizarre, but it happened as recently as last month.

Then the scheme ran out of money, it solicited R 8m from private investors to fund a car dealership, that never existed beyond paper, where the business would have been carrier forward. The cash was used to pay out csome of the investors in the car scheme.


Further information:
The scheme was the brainchild of Arrie, whose family runs the World Shakers Charismatic Church in Mable Hall.
He had six ‘agents’ who acquired customers. One of them, the almost famous AFrikaans singer Carlien.
Marks had to be credit worthy, and successfully applies for finance through Marquis, 90% of the time, it’s a small independent asset finance group underwritten by Standard Bank. The CRO of Marquis made it happen.
Marquis would approve finance for, for example, a Ford Ranger, but the dealer would inflate the price to that of a different model. Marquee would sign it off, and make the funding available. That’s how the luxury cars were bought and profits made. There never was a person on the other side renting the lower priced car.
There were 4 car dealerships, in Sandton and the East Rand, involved in the scheme. Nissan Bruma is one of them, and the employees are still there.
When the going got tough, as the scheme started running out of victims late last year, a new R 62m investment from African bank was mooted as the new finance partner for the scheme and dealership. It lured in new victims, for the R 8m dealership deal.
The scheme has now collapsed but victims are still liable for their monthly repauments. Some ar in for R 59 000 a month in instalments for cars they dont need or use.
There are about 900 victims of this scam.

Script:


VO

The exhilaration of getting behind the wheel of a luxury car… the precision engineering… the sleek lines of cutting edge design…high performance, high status.

UPS MARLENE (PRONOUNCED MARLAYN)

I'm looking at 30 to 50 of my very good friends all driving these stunning cars and everyone saying the deals are working.


VO

It’s an exclusive club… and a valuable one. The South African luxury car market is worth R 1,3 billion annually.
B7739
UPS YOUSHAN
[16:12:21] They asked me, what's my preferable car? What I want to drive? I said, If you have a mustang, I don't mind and I'll drive a mustang.




VO

For more than 150 fanatics, it was a deal too good to resist: the chance to drive a sports car at a fraction of the cost of owning one.



PAUSE




And this is how it works:

To join the club, a car is bought with finance from a lender. But the price is inflated. That car then gets shared among other members of the scheme who’ve also contributed vehicles to the pool.

The members get to drive one of these luxury models for six months at a time.

But why inflate the cost? Well, the difference between the actual price and what was borrowed is - surprise, surprise - handed to the people who dreamt up the scheme. They then pay themselves as well as the car’s instalments. Yes, how it got off the ground is a mystery to us too.




FADE OUT PAUSE
PART ONE
B7722
GLENDA
So when I looked at it, it looked and smelled like a Ponzi scheme.


VO

A ponzi scheme is only able to pay out its investors by constantly luring new ones for a steady supply of fresh cash to stay afloat - those in first, share the spoils from the newbies..

Glenda Paul is an investigator representing most of the people taken for a ride in this scam. At its centre is a company called A and A Dealings.


GLENDA
This entire scheme was set up by word of mouth, agents were sold the concept and they approached friends, families.They use this platform in order to sell the investment to the investors.


VO

In other words, the first people recruited were those who most trusted the agents. We’ll hear more about them a little later.

First, though, we need to introduce Arrie van der Berg, head honcho at A and A Dealings.

Using five agents – including a social media bodybuilding star and Afrikaans pop sensation - to provide the prospects, Arrie promised his investors the ride of their lives.

And sell his agents did. A whopping R 160 million’s worth… amounting to nearly twenty percent of the entire annual luxury vehicle market in South Africa.





PAUSE
IN FOLDER

Cordelia talking cars and excited for victim
VOICENOTE TRANSLATION

I only want the best for you guys, and there's nothing that I won't do for you, I'm so excited for you! You're going to have a new car!


VO

That excited voice belongs to Cordelia Potgieter - a popular singer whose public profile made her the perfect salesperson. We’ll hear from her a little later.


GLENDA
I think a lot of them trusted these individuals; they rely on the goodwill of the person telling them or selling them the scheme.


VO

And trust is important in a scheme this complicated. Let’s return to our earlier explanation…

The participants, who had to have a clean credit record, signed a flimsy contract with A and A Dealings, taking out finance on a new car.

We already know the price was loaded.

So, a car worth R 1 million, for example, would be financed for half a million more.

This was done by simply inflating the price on the finance deal.

The R 500 000 balance - that the investor or member is none-the-less indebted for - becomes a cash back payment to Arrie and his agents. Some of the cash is used to pay the instalments, the rest they pocket.

But here’s the kicker: the member never takes possession of the car, Arrie does, adding some vehicles to the pool, allegedly renting out the others in a separate scheme.










VO

Entrepreneur Marlene Pinto got wind of the scheme through her social circle.
B 7708
MARLENE
[12:05:10] it looked so promising and it looked so great to all of us, but once they spoke to me I decided to watch what was going on before I jumped in.
B 7708
MASA
[12:16:45] So just to backtrack, before you went into this deal, you suggested and analyzed it over six months and then in December, you get a brand new shiny.
MARLENE
[12:16:57] Yes, a stunning Maserati. I was shocked because I didn't realize they had these kind of cars in the footprint.
MASA
[12:17:22] And how much are you paying for this?
MARLENE
[12:17:24] So I didn't because it wasn't the car I purchased. I didn't pay for it at all. That would also make this whole idea so desirable for everybody.


VO
Remember, Arrie was paying the car instalments


VO
Marlene financed two high end BMW’s through the scheme. Their “real” collective value was just over three million Rand and for a while, she got to drive a R 6 million Maserati.
P1011614


LINK
I know what you must be thinking. Did they really think that they were going to drive these kinds of cars for free?


VO
It’s a question all the more mystifying when you consider many of the members wouldn’t have a paycheck to match the significant instalments.
So, for the scheme to work, that little complication had to be papered over..
Put more bluntly, their income and expenses were doctored..
B 7739
YOUSHAN
[16:15:35] somebody had to have been involved in the inside to approve these deals because there's a certain level that your disposable income can only be 30% of your financing. And a lot of people were earning salaries of 40,000 and getting financed vehicles for 29,000..
Show docs
VO

That’s a repayment of 75% of earnings.

This member, who didn’t want us to show his face, has a regular day job, with a reasonable salary. He’s divorced and doesn’t own a house.

His credit application reflected as much. Yet on the system where it eventually ended up - a banking back-end system - showed an income of two and a half times his pay, that he’s married, and owns a R 2 million house.





PAUSE AND THEN TO THE OVERLAY OF CRUZN AND NISSAN BRUMA, and then where they show Masa the docs


VO

A and A used Bruma Nissan as well as Cruzn Motors in Umhlanga as two of their dealers of choice. Both deny loading the sale price on their cars.

Bruma Nissan showed us that credit applications were captured accurately and then passed onto the bank.

So, at what point exactly, was the information doctored?


VO
Confused? Who wouldn’t be with a scheme this complex
Let’s break it down:
Arrie and his agents source a car from one of the dealerships, a prospective member applies for finance but, as we know, the price is inflated and the credit info manipulated. And hey presto, the door is opened to a car the member couldn’t otherwise afford.
And our investigation suggests the doctoring happens beyond the dealership.
A handful of the cars were financed by major banks, the majority, by an independent company called Marquis Finance.


PAUSE FOR EFFECT


VO
A Marquis Finance insider told us an executive at the company approved all applications from A and A Dealings.
That executive was head of underwriting Marcel Pieterse… the man who makes the ultimate call on whether to finance or not.
Despite admitting to being fired over the allegations, he denied any wrongdoing.
He did admit, though, to having a lifelong friendship with an A and A Dealings agent.


VO

While the going was good, the deals were streaming in, and that brings us back to Cordelia - one of Arrie’s trusted agents and not shy of the hard sell.




VOICENOTE

Good morning. I hope all is well with you and your loved ones? …… Ah, you know it's so nice to do these cars - it makes such a difference in people's lives.


VO

We had serious questions for Cordelia, but when we called, she claimed innocence..
VIDEO-2023-06-03-15-20-42


CORDELIA
This is a good deal. And I was like, okay, because this is going to a bank or whatever, Then, you know, it's illegal because they sign into the banks. And but I wasn't like, even involved in that part. Nothing at all.


VO
Yet, here’s a little excerpt from a VERY long voice note to a potential member which suggests Cordelia knew precisely how the scheme worked.
FILENAME
Explains scam with banks


VOICENOTE
Hi, dear. Sorry, but the network is bad, here where I'm driving. OK, so just to explain it to you: OK, so the financing goes through the banks, so they don't have anything to do with the monthly payments. The car gets financed, it's seen as just a normal transaction between you and the bank; it's your vehicle,and you are responsible for the payments; you sign it, you accept it, but the thing is, we pay every month - Arrie pays every month before the debit order goes off, he pays that amount into your account, and then, at the end of the year, he buys the car from you, if that's OK with you. So the finance house and the financing gets organised for you - that gets done - but that transaction has nothing to do with Arrie's arrangement with you. Arrie doesn't put it in a contract with you, because he pays for your car every month, but all [unintelligible] he can't pay one month on your car. [???] But he's never done, to the best of my understanding, as all my current clients are quite happy. And that's Arrie's side of things; that they will pay for your car every month, from their company's trust. And I get it; it sounds too good to be true, it sounds risky, but I've been on this system for two years, and my clients and I haven't encountered any problems at all. So, yeah; the finance gets done; you pay the financing; you know, every month, you do it as though it were any normal car purchase. The only difference is that Arrie pays for your car every month, and, at the end of the car, he just sells the car for you, and you can enter into a new deal with him with the financing. So yeah; that's how Arrie does it, so if anything isn't clear, just talk to me, OK?


CORDELIA
[00:06:13] I wasn't involved in any of the other stuff, you know, So I was just the middle man.
MASA
[00:06:18] It's not just the middle men. I need you to understand the gravity of the role that you played in this.
CORDELIA
[00:06:38] No, I'm trying to tell you also. I was also. I was also in. I was also believing what the people were believing. So I'm not. I'm not sure what you guys, if I can ask you, what are you trying to what are you trying to pinpoint here?
MASA
Speaker 2: [00:06:55] Yeah. I'll give you a clarity here. I'm saying to you, I understand that you're pleading ignorance here, that you didn't understand everything. Let me finish. Let me finish my point. This is going to work. If I finish my point, what I'm saying to you is I understand you saying you weren't fully involved. I need you to understand that you did have some sort of an involvement by being an agent. One to what I need you to understand is your influence and your role in this. When people see someone who is of a popular nature like yourself, who is influential, who is a part of this deal, you have some sort of a role to play that you've influenced people actively and subconsciously. So. You have? I have voice notes of you. Cordelia kept saying to people, What a great thing this is.
CORDELIA:
[00:07:44] It's a great thing. And your time is a great thing.
MASA
[00:07:46] Cordelia, for you.
CORDELIA
[00:07:51] It's going to happen. It is going to voice note because I didn't force anyone. I was. It was also a great deal for me. So we didn't do any. I didn't do anything wrong.
MASA
[00:08:01] You didn't do anything wrong by convincing people to go into a scam. [00:08:04][3.4]
Speaker 1: [00:08:05] You didn't try to, you know, listen to me. Listen to me. Convincing in signing documents. I wasn't involved in any documents. I was. It was also. [00:08:11][6.4]
Speaker 2: [00:08:11] Great. You take responsibility by you. [00:08:13][1.9]
Speaker 1: [00:08:14] What about you? But what was what responsibility do you need me to take it? Even what? Most of what I do for you guys.


VO

Everyone, except the dealerships, were ducking and diving, washing their hands of any wrongdoing.

Despite the evidence, we heard Cordelia refusing to admit that she was involved, and Juandre Beetge, another agent, did not want to talk to us because he claims A and A Dealings ruined HIS life…

But what about the pair’s victims….

As ponzis inevitably do, the whole scheme collapsed in February when the agents didn’t recruit enough people to fund the growing pool of repayments, commissions and cars.

Simply put, A and A Dealings ran out of money.


YOUSHAN
[16:12:49] Arrie sent a message out to a few of us notifying us that their bank accounts had been frozen. And we should we shouldn't worry about anything


SLIGHT BREATHER


VO

Arrie went quiet. and, because he no longer paid the instalments on the victim’s financed vehicles as he promised, the banks are now going after the victims of the scheme.

After all, the cars were financed in their names.


MARLENE

[12:27:36] my life has actually been turned upside down. I actually don't even know what to do.


VO

Most of the victims are liable for repayments between 50 and 90 000 Rand a month.


MARLENE
People are not paying their bonds, trying to pay a little bit to the bank. That's about 300 people that this is going to change people's lives in a negative way forever


VO

Wesbank and Marquis Finance declined to talk to us citing internal investigations.

Arrie sent us a letter through his lawyers saying he’s not talking. ,
B 7739
YOUSHAN
[16:21:48] Life lessons, uh, when something is too good to be true? Definitely. I'll go with that.

VO For more than 150 fanatics, it was a deal too good to resist: the chance to drive a sports car at a fraction of the cost of owning one. PAUSE And this is how it works: To join the club, a car is bought with finance from a lender. But the price is inflated. That car then gets shared among other members of the scheme who’ve also contributed vehicles to the pool. The members get to drive one of these luxury models for six months at a time. But why inflate the cost? Well, the difference between the actual price and what was borrowed is - surprise, surprise - handed to the people who dreamt up the scheme. They then pay themselves as well as the car’s instalments. Yes, how it got off the ground is a mystery to us too. FADE OUT PAUSE PART ONE B7722 GLENDA So when I looked at it, it looked and smelled like a Ponzi scheme. VO A ponzi scheme is only able to pay out its investors by constantly luring new ones for a steady supply of fresh cash to stay afloat - those in first, share the spoils from the newbies.. Glenda Paul is an investigator representing most of the people taken for a ride in this scam. At its centre is a company called A and A Dealings. GLENDA This entire scheme was set up by word of mouth, agents were sold the concept and they approached friends, families.They use this platform in order to sell the investment to the investors. VO In other words, the first people recruited were those who most trusted the agents. We’ll hear more about them a little later. First, though, we need to introduce Arrie van der Berg, head honcho at A and A Dealings. Using five agents – including a social media bodybuilding star and Afrikaans pop sensation - to provide the prospects, Arrie promised his investors the ride of their lives. And sell his agents did. A whopping R 160 million’s worth… amounting to nearly twenty percent of the entire annual luxury vehicle market in South Africa. Let’s return to our earlier explanation… The participants, who had to have a clean credit record, signed a flimsy contract with A and A Dealings, taking out finance on a new car. We already know the price was loaded. So, a car worth R 1 million, for example, would be financed for half a million more. This was done by simply inflating the price on the finance deal. The R 500 000 balance - that the investor or member is none-the-less indebted for - becomes a cash back payment to Arrie and his agents. Some of the cash is used to pay the instalments, the rest they pocket. But here’s the kicker: the member never takes possession of the car, Arrie does, adding some vehicles to the pool, allegedly renting out the others in a separate scheme. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): we investigate how a luxury car scam fleeced almost R 200 million from victim's pockets.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Its a multi layered ponzi and fraud scheme, it's sexy and driven by status, ego and cash... a festival of robbing Peter to pay Paul and then robbing Paul to pay another.
metadata.Summary: It’s fraud, on a grand scale. Two schemes so elaborate and hundreds of millions of Rand that have magically disappeared. Imagine driving a luxury car, like an Aston Martin, and you do not have to pay the massive instalments that goes with it. Now imagine, that you get to drive an Aston Martin this month, a Ferrari the next, and a Porche the month after that. For 900 investors, this was their dream come true. All they had to do was ‘buy’ a middleweight car, which was ‘rented out’ to someone else, that covered off the instalments, and the luxury car experience was theirs….. It sounds bizarre, but it happened as recently as last month. Then the scheme ran out of money, it solicited R 8m from private investors to fund a car dealership, that never existed beyond paper, where the business would have been carrier forward. The cash was used to pay out csome of the investors in the car scheme.
metadata.Further information: The scheme was the brainchild of Arrie, whose family runs the World Shakers Charismatic Church in Mable Hall. He had six ‘agents’ who acquired customers. One of them, the almost famous AFrikaans singer Carlien. Marks had to be credit worthy, and successfully applies for finance through Marquis, 90% of the time, it’s a small independent asset finance group underwritten by Standard Bank. The CRO of Marquis made it happen. Marquis would approve finance for, for example, a Ford Ranger, but the dealer would inflate the price to that of a different model. Marquee would sign it off, and make the funding available. That’s how the luxury cars were bought and profits made. There never was a person on the other side renting the lower priced car. There were 4 car dealerships, in Sandton and the East Rand, involved in the scheme. Nissan Bruma is one of them, and the employees are still there. When the going got tough, as the scheme started running out of victims late last year, a new R 62m investment from African bank was mooted as the new finance partner for the scheme and dealership. It lured in new victims, for the R 8m dealership deal. The scheme has now collapsed but victims are still liable for their monthly repauments. Some ar in for R 59 000 a month in instalments for cars they dont need or use. There are about 900 victims of this scam.
